translation_en: Abu Kurayb narrated to me; Abu Usamah narrated to us; Burayd narrated to us, from Abu Burdah, who said: I arrived in Madinah, and Abdullah ibn Salam met me. He said, “Come to the house so I can give you a drink in a cup from which the Messenger of Allah drank, and so you can pray in a mosque where the Prophet prayed.” I went with him. He gave me a drink of sawiq, fed me dates, and I prayed in his mosque.

Said ibn al-Rabi narrated to us; Ali ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir; Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, that Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, told him: The Prophet told me: “A visitor came to me tonight from my Lord while I was at al-Aqiq and said, ‘Pray in this blessed valley, and say: an umrah and a pilgrimage.’” Harun ibn Ismail said: Ali narrated to us the wording, “an umrah within a pilgrimage.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar: The Prophet designated Qarn for the people of Najd, al-Juhfah for the people of Syria, and Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah as their points for entering consecration. He said: I heard this from the Prophet, and I was told that the Prophet also said, “For the people of Yemen, Yalamlam.” Iraq was mentioned, and he said, “There was no Iraq at that time.”

Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us; al-Fudayl narrated to us; Musa ibn Uqbah narrated to us; Salim ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from his father, from the Prophet: He was shown a vision while he was at his resting place in Dhu al-Hulayfah, and it was said to him, “You are in a blessed valley.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad informed us; Abdullah informed us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Prophet, during the dawn prayer, raise his head from bowing and say: “Our Lord, praise is Yours in the Hereafter.” Then he said: “O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so.” Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: “You have no part in the decision—or He may turn to them in mercy or punish them, for they are wrongdoers” (3:128).

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. (Another chain:) Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to me; Attab ibn Bashir informed us, from Ishaq, from al-Zuhri. Ali ibn Husayn informed me that Husayn ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, told him that Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of Allah came to him and Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah, at night and said to them, “Will you not pray?” Ali said: I replied, “Messenger of Allah, our souls are in Allah’s hand; when He wishes to wake us, He will wake us.” The Messenger of Allah turned away when I said that and did not reply. Then I heard him, as he walked away, striking his thigh and saying: “The human being is the most argumentative of things” (18:54). Abu Abdullah said: Anything that comes to you at night is called tariq. The word tariq can also mean a star; thaqib means shining. One says, “Make your fire burn brightly,” to someone tending a fire.

Qutaybah narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Said, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While we were in the mosque, the Messenger of Allah came out and said, “Let us go to the Jews.” We went with him until we came to their school. The Prophet stood and called to them: “O community of Jews, accept Islam and you will be safe.” They said, “You have conveyed the message, Abu al-Qasim.” The Messenger of Allah said, “That is what I want: accept Islam and you will be safe.” They again said, “You have conveyed the message, Abu al-Qasim.” The Messenger of Allah said, “That is what I want.” Then he said it a third time and said: “Know that the land belongs to Allah and His Messenger, and I intend to expel you from this land. Whoever among you owns property may sell it; otherwise, know that the land belongs to Allah and His Messenger.”

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Said al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “Noah will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and asked, ‘Did you convey the message?’ He will say, ‘Yes, my Lord.’ His people will then be asked, ‘Did a warner come to you?’ They will say, ‘No warner came to us.’ He will be asked, ‘Who are your witnesses?’ He will say, ‘Muhammad and his community.’ You will then be brought and will testify.” Then the Messenger of Allah recited: “Thus We have made you a balanced community” (2:143), meaning just, “so that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you.” Jafar ibn Awn also reported this from al-Amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Said al-Khudri, from the Prophet.

Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us; Haywah narrated to us; Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Had informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, from Busayr ibn Said, from Abu Qays, the freedman of Amr ibn al-As, from Amr ibn al-As, who heard the Messenger of Allah say: “When a judge gives a ruling and exercises his judgment, then is correct, he receives two rewards. If he gives a ruling and exercises his judgment, then is mistaken, he receives one reward.” I related this hadith to Abu Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm, who said, “Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated it to me from Abu Hurayrah in the same way.” Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muttalib reported it from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Abu Salamah, from the Prophet, with the same meaning.

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj; Ata narrated to me, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Abu Musa asked Umar for permission to enter. It seemed Umar was occupied, so Abu Musa went back. Umar said, “Did I not hear the voice of Abdullah ibn Qays? Let him in.” Abu Musa was called back. Umar asked, “What made you do that?” He replied, “We were instructed to do this.” Umar said, “Bring me proof of this, or I will deal with you.” Abu Musa went to a gathering of the Ansar. They said, “Only the youngest among us will testify.” Abu Said al-Khudri stood and said, “We were instructed to do this.” Umar said, “This matter of the Prophet had been hidden from me; buying and selling in the markets distracted me.”

Ali narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us; al-Zuhri narrated to me, who heard it from al-Araj. He said: Abu Hurayrah informed me: You claim that Abu Hurayrah narrates many hadiths from the Messenger of Allah. Allah is the ultimate judge between us. I was a poor man who stayed close to the Messenger of Allah to fill my stomach, while the Emigrants were occupied with buying and selling in the markets and the Ansar were occupied with managing their property. One day I was present with the Messenger of Allah, and he said: “Whoever spreads out his cloak until I finish speaking, then gathers it up, will never forget anything he hears from me.” I spread out the mantle I was wearing. By the One who sent him with the truth, I never forgot anything I heard from him.

Hammad ibn Humayd narrated to us; Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to us; my father narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Sad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I saw Jabir ibn Abdullah swear by Allah that Ibn al-Sa’id was the Dajjal. I said, “Do you swear by Allah?” He said, “I heard Umar swear to that in the presence of the Prophet, and the Prophet did not object.”

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Horses are of three kinds: for one man they are a reward, for another they are a means of protection, and for another they are a burden of sin. The one for whom they are a reward is a man who ties them in the path of Allah and lets them graze for a long time in a pasture or garden. Whatever they eat within the length of their tether from that pasture or garden is counted as good deeds for him. If they break their tether and run up a hill or two, their hoofprints and dung are good deeds for him. If they pass by a river and drink from it, even though he did not intend to water them there, that too is counted as good deeds for him, and he receives a reward for them. Another man ties horses to preserve his wealth and maintain his dignity, while not forgetting Allah’s right concerning their necks and backs; they are protection for him. A third man ties horses out of pride and showing off; they are a burden of sin for him.” The Messenger of Allah was asked about donkeys. He said: “Nothing was revealed to me concerning them except this all-encompassing verse: ‘Whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it’” (99:7–8).

Yahya narrated to us; Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Safiyyah, from his mother, from Aishah: A woman asked the Prophet. (Another chain:) Muhammad—that is, Ibn Uqbah—narrated to us; al-Fudayl ibn Sulayman al-Numayri al-Basri narrated to us; Mansur ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Shaybah narrated to us; my mother narrated to me, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: A woman asked the Prophet how to wash after menstruation. He said: “Take a piece of cloth scented with musk and cleanse yourself with it.” She asked, “How should I cleanse myself with it, Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Cleanse yourself with it.” She again asked, “How should I cleanse myself with it, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Cleanse yourself with it.” Aishah said: I understood what the Messenger of Allah meant, so I pulled her toward me and explained it to her.

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: Umm Hufayd, daughter of al-Harith ibn Hazn, gave the Prophet clarified butter, dried yogurt, and lizards. The Prophet called for them, and they were eaten at his table. He left them, disliking them. Had they been forbidden, they would not have been eaten at his table, nor would he have ordered that they be eaten.

Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to us; Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab. Ata ibn Abi Rabah informed me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Prophet said: “Whoever eats garlic or onions should keep away from us—or keep away from our mosque—and stay in his house.” A dish was brought to him—(Ibn Wahb said it means a tray)—containing green vegetables. He smelled an odor from it and asked about it. He was told which vegetables it contained. He said, “Bring it near,” and it was brought near to one of the Companions who was with him. When he saw that the Prophet disliked eating it, he said, “Eat, for I converse privately with One with whom you do not converse.” Ibn Ufayr reported from Ibn Wahb that it was a pot containing green vegetables. Al-Layth and Abu Safwan did not mention the pot story in their reports from Yunus, so I do not know whether it was al-Zuhri’s own statement or part of the hadith.

Ubaydullah ibn Sad ibn Ibrahim narrated to me; my father and my uncle narrated to us; they both said: My father narrated to us, from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr informed me that his father, Jubayr ibn Mutim, told him: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah and spoke to him about something. He gave her an instruction. She said, “What do you think, Messenger of Allah, if I do not find you?” He said: “If you do not find me, then go to Abu Bakr.” Al-Humaydi added, from Ibrahim ibn Sad, that she seemed to mean his death.

Abu al-Yaman said: Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that he heard Muawiyah speaking to a group of Quraysh in Madinah. He mentioned Kab al-Ahbar and said: “If he is among the most truthful of those who narrate reports from the People of the Book, we nevertheless sometimes find lies in what he tells us.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me; Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us; Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah said: “Do not affirm the People of the Book, and do not deny them. Rather say: ‘We believe in Allah and what was sent down to us and what was sent down to you’” (2:136), and continue the verse.

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Ibrahim narrated to us; Ibn Shihab informed us, from Ubaydullah, that Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: “How can you ask the People of the Book about anything when your Book, which was sent down to the Messenger of Allah, is more recent? You read it pure, unmixed. He has told you that the People of the Book altered Allah’s Book, changed it, and wrote a book with their own hands, then said, ‘This is from Allah,’ in order to obtain a small price. Is the knowledge that has come to you not enough to stop you from asking them? By Allah, we have never seen one of them ask you about what was sent down to you.”

Ishaq narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sallam ibn Abi Muti, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Jundab ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “Recite the Quran as long as your hearts are in agreement. When you disagree, leave it.” Abu Abdullah said: Abd al-Rahman heard Sallam.

Ishaq narrated to us; Abd al-Samad informed us; Hammam narrated to us; Abu Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Jundab ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Recite the Quran as long as your hearts are in agreement about it. When you disagree, leave it.” Yazid ibn Harun reported from Harun al-Awar: Abu Imran narrated to us, from Jundab, from the Prophet.

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us; Hisham informed us, from Mamar, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet’s final illness approached—and there were men in the house, including Umar ibn al-Khattab—he said: “Come, let me write a document for you, after which you will never go astray.” Umar said: “The Prophet is overcome by pain, and you have the Quran; the Book of Allah is sufficient for us.” The members of the household disagreed and argued. Some said, “Bring the writing materials so that the Messenger of Allah can write a document for you, after which you will never go astray.” Others said what Umar had said. When they argued loudly and disagreed in the presence of the Prophet, he said: “Get up and leave me.” Ubaydullah said: Ibn Abbas used to say, “The calamity, the whole calamity, was the disagreement and noise that came between the Messenger of Allah and his writing that document for them.”

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata said that Jabir said. Abu Abdullah said: Muhammad ibn Bakr reported to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata informed me; I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say, in the presence of a group with him: We, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, entered consecration for pilgrimage alone, without an umrah with it. The Prophet arrived on the morning of the fourth day of Dhu al-Hijjah. When we arrived, the Prophet ordered us to leave consecration and said: “Leave consecration and be intimate with your wives.” Ata said that Jabir said: He did not insist on this, but permitted it for them. He heard that we were saying: “There are only five days between us and Arafah, yet he ordered us to leave consecration and return to our wives, so that we will go to Arafah with our male organs dripping with semen.” Jabir gestured with his hand as he said this. The Messenger of Allah stood and said: “You know that I am the most God-fearing of you, the most truthful, and the most dutiful. Were it not that I brought sacrificial animals, I would leave consecration as you do. So leave consecration. If I had known beforehand what I later came to know, I would not have brought sacrificial animals.” So we left consecration, heard, and obeyed.

Abu Mamar narrated to us; Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Ibn Buraydah, who said: Abdullah al-Muzani told me, from the Prophet, who said: “Pray before the sunset prayer”—on the third time he added—“for whoever wishes.” He said this because he disliked people taking it as a regular practice.

Al-Uwaysi narrated to us; Ibrahim narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab. Urwah, Ibn al-Musayyab, Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and Ubaydullah narrated to me, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her. When the people of the slander spoke against her, she said: When revelation was delayed, the Messenger of Allah called Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd and consulted them about separating from his wife. Usamah advised him based on what he knew of his wife’s innocence. Ali said, “Allah has not made things difficult for you; there are many women besides her. Ask the slave girl and she will tell you the truth.” He said, “Have you seen anything that makes you suspicious?” She said, “I have seen nothing beyond the fact that she is a young girl who sometimes falls asleep while kneading her family’s dough, and the domestic animal comes and eats it.” The Prophet stood on the pulpit and said: “O Muslims, who will excuse me regarding a man whose harm concerning my family has reached me? By Allah, I know nothing but good about my family.” Then he spoke of Aishah’s innocence. Abu Usamah reported it from Hisham.

Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to me; Yahya ibn Abi Zakariyya al-Ghassani narrated to us, from Hisham, from Urwah, from Aishah: The Messenger of Allah addressed the people, praised and glorified Allah, and said: “What do you advise me concerning people who speak abusively about my family? I have never known any evil of them.” Urwah said: When Aishah was told what had happened, she said, “Messenger of Allah, may I go to my family?” He gave her permission and sent the young servant with her. A man from the Ansar said, “Glory be to You! It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander.”
Abu Asim narrated to us; Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Sayfi, from Abu Mabd, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet sent Muadh to Yemen.

Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to me; al-Fadl ibn al-Ala narrated to us; Ismail ibn Umayyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sayfi, who heard Abu Mabd, the freedman of Ibn Abbas, say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: When the Prophet sent Muadh toward Yemen, he said to him: “You are going to a people from among the People of the Book. Let the first thing you call them to be that they worship Allah alone. When they recognize that, tell them that Allah has made five prayers obligatory upon them during each day and night. When they perform them, tell them that Allah has made charity obligatory upon their wealth, taken from their rich and returned to their poor. When they acknowledge that, take it from them, but avoid taking the best of people’s wealth.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Ghundar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Abu Husayn and al-Ashath ibn Sulaym, who both heard al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Muadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Prophet said: “Muadh, do you know Allah’s right over His servants?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “That they worship Him and associate nothing with Him. Do you know their right upon Him?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “That He does not punish them.”
